units.source_text: 柏木所说的事或许是真的，他说，改变世界的，不是行动而是认识，并且是一味模仿行动到了极限的认识。

en.t: What Kashiwagi said may have been true: he said that what changes the world is not action but recognition, and moreover a kind of recognition that imitates action single-mindedly until it reaches its limit.

units.source_text: 我的认识就是属于这种类型的，并且是一种使行动真的变成无效的认识。

en.t: My own recognition belonged precisely to that type, and it was a recognition that truly rendered action ineffective.

units.source_text: 如此看来，我长期以来的精心准备，岂不是完全为了"无需行动也行"的这种最后的认识吗？

en.t: Seen in that light, had all my careful preparations over these many years not been entirely for this final recognition that action was not necessary after all?
